'./http.js';\n\n// A tiny HTTP router. Routes are registered with .get() / .post() and matched in\n// registration order. The first route with a matching method and URL wins, and\n// its captured path segments are passed to the handler as positional arguments.\n//\n// Routing preserves the original behavior of the cumulative evaluator suite:\n//   - It uses only Node.js 26 built-ins (`node:http`, `node:sqlite`, `node:crypto`) and plain JavaScript modules.\n\n## Starting the server\n\n```bash\nPORT=3000 ./run.sh\n```\n\n`run.sh` runs `node server.js` in the foreground. The server binds to `127.0.0.1` and reads the port from the `PORT` environment variable, defaulting to `3000`.\n\nVerify it is up:\n\n```bash\ncurl http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/health\n# {\"ok\":true}\n```\n\n## Entry point and major files\n\n- **`server.js`** — Entry point. Creates the HTTP server, wires the route table via `lib/router.js`, and starts listening. It also calls `db.initDb()` at startup.\n- **`lib/router.js`** — Minimal HTTP router. Routes are registered in order and matched by method and regex. Captured path segments are passed to handlers as positional arguments.\n- **`lib/db.js`** — Persistence layer. Owns the SQLite `DatabaseSync` connection, the schema, and all CRUD operations.\n- **`lib/domain.js`** — Pure business logic: dice parsing, encounter XP, initiative ordering, character modifiers, auth hashing, and validation helpers.\n- **`lib/http.js`** — Shared HTTP utilities: body reading, JSON responses, and common error helpers.\n- **`lib/handlers.js`** — HTTP request handlers, organized by domain (health, storage, auth, dice, characters, PHB rules, combat, compendium, campaigns, and DM helpers).\n- **`run.sh`** — Foreground startup script.\n\n## State, persistence, and routing\n\n### Persistence\n\n- SQLite database file: `game.db` in the project root.\n- Schema version is fixed at `1` and exposed via `/v1/storage/status`.\n- Tables: `users`, `combat_sessions`, `monsters`, `items`, `campaigns`, `characters`, `events`.\n- JSON arrays/objects (initiative order, combat conditions, monster tags) are serialized to TEXT columns with `JSON.stringify`/`JSON.parse`.\n- `/v1/storage/reset` drops and recreates all tables; this is the only destructive endpoint and is intended for tests.\n\n### Request routing\n\n`server.js` builds a `Router` from `lib/router.js`. Routes are evaluated in registration order, and the first matching method/pattern wins. Parameterized routes are placed before general ones so they are not accidentally shadowed.\n\nThe router preserves the following behavior, which the cumulative evaluator suite depends on:\n\n- `GET` without a matching route returns `405 Method Not Allowed` and does not read the body.\n- `POST` without a matching route reads the body, then returns `404 Not Found`.\n- Any other HTTP method returns `405 Method Not Allowed` without reading the body.\n\n`POST` handlers receive the raw body on `req.body` as a string; handlers parse it with `lib/http.js::parseJson`.\n\n## API / domain groupings\n\n| Group | Endpoints | Purpose |\n|-------|-----------|---------|\n| **Health** | `GET /health` | Liveness check. |\n| **Storage** | `GET /v1/storage/status`, `POST /v1/storage/reset` | SQLite status and reset. |\n| **Auth** | `POST /v1/auth/register`, `POST /v1/auth/login` | User accounts with `scrypt` password hashing. |\n| **Core / Dice** | `POST /v1/dice/stats`, `POST /v1/checks/ability`, `POST /v1/encounters/adjusted-xp`, `POST /v1/initiative/order` | Dice stats, ability checks, encounter XP, initiative. |\n| **Characters** | `POST /v1/characters/ability-modifier`, `POST /v1/characters/proficiency`, `POST /v1/characters/derived-stats` | Character modifiers and derived stats. |\n| **PHB Rules** | `POST /v1/phb/spell-slots`, `POST /v1/phb/rests/long`, `POST /v1/phb/equipment-load` | Spell slots, long rest, carrying capacity. |\n| **Combat** | `POST /v1/combat/sessions`, `POST /v1/combat/sessions/:id/conditions`, `POST /v1/combat/sessions/:id/advance` | Create session, add conditions, advance turns. |\n| **Compendium** | `POST /v1/compendium/monsters`, `GET /v1/compendium/monsters/:slug`, `POST /v1/compendium/items`, `GET /v1/compendium/items/:slug` | Monster and item reference entries. |\n| **Campaigns** | `POST /v1/campaigns`, `POST /v1/campaigns/:id/characters`, `POST /v1/campaigns/:id/events`, `GET /v1/campaigns/:id/state` | Campaigns, characters, and session log. |\n| **DM Helpers** | `POST /v1/dm/encounter-builder`, `POST /v1/dm/loot-parcel`, `POST /v1/dm/session-recap` | DM-facing convenience tools. |\n\n## Conventions for extending and testing the codebase\n\n- **Keep handlers thin**: handlers validate input, call `lib/db.js` or `lib/domain.js`, and format responses. Business rules belong in `lib/domain.js`.\n- **Add routes in order**: new routes go into the `createRouter()` chain in `server.js` in the order they should be checked. Place parameterized routes before general ones that could shadow them.\n- **Use the existing validation helpers**: prefer `isNonEmptyString`, `isPositiveInteger`, `isNonNegativeInteger`, `isValidSlug`, and `isStringArray` for consistent error messages.\n- **Preserve response shapes**: existing endpoints have fixed response bodies required by the cumulative test suite. Any changes must keep status codes and JSON keys identical.\n- **JSON bodies**: all handlers use `requireBody` from `lib/handlers.js`, which wraps `lib/http.js::parseJson`. Invalid JSON returns `400 invalid json`.\n- **Errors**: `badRequest` → `400 { error }`, `unauthorized` → `401 { error }`, `notFound` → `404 { error: 'not found' }`, `methodNotAllowed` → `405 { error: 'method not allowed' }`, `conflict` → `409 { error }`. Parameterized routes are placed before more general parents so they are not accidentally shadowed.\n\nThe router preserves the following behavior, which the cumulative evaluator suite depends on:\n\n- `GET` without a matching route returns `405 Method Not Allowed` and does not read the body.\n- `POST` without a matching route reads the body, then returns `404 Not Found`.\n- Any other HTTP method returns `405 Method Not Allowed` without reading the body.\n\n`POST` handlers receive the raw body on `req.body` as a string.
